title: Habib: Two Rings, Zero Trades, and a Dynasty Waiting on One More Comeback
body: Every league has a founding dynasty, and the Buckaroo Football League's is the Habibsters. Kaushal opened the league's history in 2023 by going 10-4, scoring 1,528.8 points, locking up the 1 seed and winning Buckaroo Bowl I. It wasn't always pretty: his worst week ever, a 74.5-point dud against Sonny in Week 9, came during that championship season. Champions don't need to be perfect, apparently. They just need to be holding the trophy in December.

Then Habib did it again. The 2024 Habibsters went 11-3, put up 1,524.8 points, took the 1 seed for the second straight year and won Buckaroo Bowl II, making Kaushal the only manager in the league's first two seasons to know what a parade felt like. Spend enough time on a UGA fan's couch and you learn that some people think repeat titles are just the natural order of things. For two years, the Buckaroo Football League couldn't argue.

2025 was the year the luck turned. The Habibsters scored a career-high 1,973.6 points across a longer 16-week slate, including the best single week of Kaushal's career, a 151.5-point blowout of Ramon in Week 2. Somehow that added up to only an 8-8 record. He still made the playoffs as the 3 seed and finished third, and his only playoff loss in league history came that year, leaving him 4-1 in the postseason overall. That's the kind of record that gets a guy's number retired, if fantasy leagues retired numbers.

The head-to-head ledger reads like a hit list. Habibi owns Mekhi 9-2, which has to sting for the guy who probably knows more football than anyone in the league. He's 7-2 against Philly and 8-4 against Brucie, asterisk games included. Sonny has kept it close at 6-5, and Randy is the only longtime rival with a winning record against him at 6-5. The newcomers have split: JMoney is 0-1 against him, while Zoe beat him in their only meeting, so Z² already holds a lead in a series the rest of the league has spent years losing.

His habits as a manager are as consistent as his early trophy count. Kaushal has made zero trades in four seasons, with no counteroffers and no blockbusters. He builds through the wire instead, with 16 pickups in 2023, 32 in 2024, 29 in 2025 and 20 already in 2026. That puts this year's Habibsters at 3-4 with 797.8 points and 14% title odds, which is not where a two-time champion expects to be in midseason. Then again, he's already shown he can make the playoffs when the record looks ordinary, and the rest of the league knows it would be unwise to count Habib out.
